title: Foundations: Operetta Style - The Complete Guide
summary: What Operetta Style is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Operetta Style songs: Vocal standards are the great interpreters' art: art songs, chanson, torch songs, and showtunes sung with classical control and emotional directness. The song is the star; the singer serves it.

History: From Schubert's lieder through Édith Piaf's chanson, Billie Holiday's torch songs, and Broadway's golden age (1943–1964), the standard repertoire rewards singers who can act a lyric.

How the songs work: Operetta Style favors the keys of F, Eb, Bb, C, G. Common forms include AABA showtune form; Through-composed art songs. Players should master legit vocal technique: breath, placement, diction first, then acting the lyric: every word means something. Piano and orchestra territory.

title: Auld Lang Syne - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Auld Lang Syne, a public-domain Operetta Style standard.
body:
Auld Lang Syne (Robert Burns, 1788. Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Should auld acquaintance be forgot,
And never brought to mind?
Should auld acquaintance be forgot,
And auld lang syne?

Chorus:
For auld lang syne, my dear,
For auld lang syne,
We'll take a cup o' kindness yet,
For auld lang syne.
